source.title: On the Power of Over-parametrization in Neural Networks with Quadratic Activation

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical generalization bounds for a weight-decayed quadratic-activation network, using a different method from the empirical versions; it does not test the versions' specific claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds, not empirical training and test errors, random-label fits, width sweeps, or measured network properties. No result tests a listed version. The bounds are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study proves optimization and generalization bounds for quadratic-activation networks with weight decay. Neither these bounds nor its optimization results establish any listed version: a width-independent upper bound does not show that test error decreases with width.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors prove benign optimization landscapes for shallow quadratic networks with fixed all-one output weights when k ≥ d, or almost surely with an arbitrarily small objective perturbation when k(k+1)/2 > n. They derive generalization bounds using norm control from weight decay and assumptions on the input distribution.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides theoretical analysis of quadratic-activation networks and weight decay rather than the empirical training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The stated generalization bounds depend on input assumptions: bounded inputs give a bound involving b²√(log d/n), while Gaussian inputs give a bound involving √(d/n) when n ≥ d log d.

fits_no_version.finding: For quadratic-activation networks with bounded Frobenius norm, the study derives generalization-gap bounds under bounded-input or Gaussian-input assumptions. These bounds have no explicit dependence on hidden-layer width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Norm control and input-distribution assumptions can yield width-independent generalization-gap bounds for quadratic-activation networks.

record.problems: The generalization findings are theoretical bounds rather than observed errors; they depend on assumptions about the input distribution and loss. No empirical comparison of training and test error is reported.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Whether test error keeps decreasing as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of locality.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparative ranking performance.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own gate note. Generalization bounds and benign optimization landscapes do not, by themselves, test the specified empirical claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance are not studied.
No test-error comparison across widths or interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of gap rankings.
